subject: To many segments and QC in SNP6 analysis

messages.author: 3c86468e768657ff
messages.subject: To many segments and QC in SNP6 analysis
parts:
I have an experiment with 101 Afymetrix SNP6 samples. The analysis
worked fine following the steps in the vignette. But for some samples
when looking at the chromosome explorer there is a very high
variability resulting in a high number of segments (10000-25000 vs.
100-1000 for the rest). The segments are distributed over all
chromosomes. You can find an example image at
http://imiblinux05.uni-muenster.de/segmentation.png

Does anyone have an explanation, what might went wrong with these
samples or how to identify and filter out these samples in a previous
step? The density and PMA/PMB plots look very similar to the ones from
the other samples.

Thanks,
Christian

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8

On Fri, Jan 21, 2011 at 2:38 AM, cruckert <cruc...@uni-muenster.de> wrote:
> I have an experiment with 101 Afymetrix SNP6 samples. The analysis
> worked fine following the steps in the vignette. But for some samples
> when looking at the chromosome explorer there is a very high
> variability resulting in a high number of segments (10000-25000 vs.
> 100-1000 for the rest). The segments are distributed over all
> chromosomes. You can find an example image at
> http://imiblinux05.uni-muenster.de/segmentation.png
>
> Does anyone have an explanation, what might went wrong with these
> samples or how to identify and filter out these samples in a previous
> step? The density and PMA/PMB plots look very similar to the ones from
> the other samples.

That is probably an issue with the DNA target/sample hybridized to the
array and not an computation/analysis problem. I doubt you can "fix"
this by statistical methods. I've seen similar problems/profiles in a
few CN samples from the TCGA project - and the "broken" profile was
very reproducible across Affymetrix, Illumina and Agilent each
processed by a different group/lab. They all got the DNA from the
same collection center. We never bothered to track down the reason
for this, that is, we don't know if it is biological, the DNA extract
or similar, but at least we know it was nothing the different labs
could fix.

In your case, if you rehybridize the same DNA sample and you get the
same profile, you will know that it is a true signal in the DNA
sample. From there you need to "troubleshoot" by other means to
figure out what the reason is.

Hope this helps

Henrik
